title: Basilicata pumps Italy's oil — and still pays above the national average
dek: The region that hosts Italy's largest onshore oilfield is charging 1.4 cents more than the country for a litre of self-service petrol, and its week-long price slide just reversed.
body: On 12 August, self-service petrol in Basilicata averaged €2.0116 per litre against a national self-service average of €1.9977 — a premium of about 1.4 cents. Diesel tells the same story: €2.1180 locally versus €2.1063 nationally, roughly 1.2 cents above the country. It is a small gap in absolute terms, but a persistent one, and it sits oddly with the fact that the Val d'Agri fields beneath these hills produce more crude than anywhere else on Italian soil. Basilicata's LPG figure is the outlier in the other direction and then some: €0.8140 self-service against €0.7567 nationally, nearly 6 cents dearer, and pinned to that exact value in every single one of the 23 days the dashboard has tracked.

The more interesting movement is the turn. Petrol in Basilicata peaked at €2.0242 on 4 August and then fell for seven consecutive days to €2.0102 on 11 August; diesel did the same from €2.1419 on 5 August down to €2.1151. On 12 August both reversed — petrol up 0.14 cents, diesel up 0.29 cents — ending the slide on the same day. Behind those averages is a small and very stable network: 267 registered stations in the region, 238 of them reporting a price yesterday. That 89% participation rate has not budged in over three weeks, and it runs just under the national figure of 21,679 reporting out of 23,957 registered.

Noticing that a seven-day decline broke on a particular Wednesday, in one region of 267 stations, is not the sort of thing anyone does by hand. It only works because the whole pipeline reruns itself every morning: pull the MIMIT export, reprocess roughly 93,000 price rows across nearly 24,000 stations, recompute the regional aggregates, rotate to the next region, and rebuild the site. Fuel Dashboard was built with Claude Code precisely so that step is automatic — a spreadsheet updated by hand gets abandoned by week three, whereas this one is on day 23 and has never missed.
pull_quote: Seven straight days of falling prices in Basilicata ended yesterday — petrol and diesel both turned upward on the same day.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Basilicata, where self-service petrol averages €2.0116 a litre — about 1.4 cents above the national average of €1.9977.

That's a quietly strange number. Basilicata sits on top of Val d'Agri, the largest onshore oilfield in Italy. Producing the crude apparently does nothing for what you pay at the pump. Diesel follows the same pattern at €2.1180 locally versus €2.1063 nationally, and LPG is nearly 6 cents dearer than the national average.

There's also a turn worth flagging. Petrol in Basilicata had fallen for seven consecutive days from its 4 August peak of €2.0242. Yesterday it ticked back up, and diesel did the same on the same day. Across the region's 267 registered stations, 238 reported a price — an 89% participation rate that has been rock-steady for three weeks.

Fuel Dashboard tracks all four fuels across all 20 Italian regions using the official MIMIT daily price export — around 93,000 price rows from nearly 24,000 stations, reprocessed every morning. Have a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

The part I'd argue for: I built this with Claude Code, and that is the only reason it still exists. A manual Excel sheet with this data would have been abandoned by week three — someone has to download the export, clean it, recompute the aggregates, redraw the charts, every single day, forever. Instead the whole pipeline reruns itself and republishes the site. The AI tooling didn't just write the code faster; it made a self-maintaining thing feasible for one person, which is a different category of project than a spreadsheet you promise yourself you'll keep updated.
